text:
Simon Holmstrom is getting the kind of chance that changes a career. Injuries to Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie have pushed him to about 20 minutes a night over his last ten games, and he's on the ice for 46% of the Islanders' power-play chances, up from 19% last season. At 25, our numbers tag him as a breakout.

The production is following. He has nine points in 16 games and his own chances are up to 0.92 expected goals per 60 from 0.66. The warning is shooting: 17.2% is above what we think he'll sustain, and our "plays like" comparisons note that chances against pile up with him on the ice too. Sixteen games is a small sample; ice time settles faster than scoring does.

There's a lot to like underneath. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.2 wins last season, with about two goals of that from drawing more penalties than he takes, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows he carries the puck in on 57% of his entries. Tonight in San Jose he's one of our Sleepers, at 52% for a point.
headline: Holmstrom's big opportunity
